newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia stocks end mixed, local factors eclipse Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Asia stocks end mixed, local factors eclipse Wall St.

text.p: Asia stock markets ended with modest gains and losses on Tuesday as local factors, such as political uncertainties in Taiwan and Thailand, eclipsed another record close on Wall Street.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average powered ahead 123 points, or 1.7 percent, on Monday to end at 7,293, the 18th record close so far this year.
The advance helped bolster some Asia markets, such as Japan, in early trade, but the momentum later fizzled out.
Recent forecasts of a U.S. economic slowdown have taken the steam out of the dollar's advance, particularly against the yen.
Traders are taking a cautious approach to a spate of U.S. economic figures due this week to see how they could influence a meeting of the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee on May 20.
Steadiness in the yen/dollar rate initially stimulated buying in major high-tech shares, but the move failed to garner support.

By the close in Tokyo, the Nikkei was off 14.40 points, or 0.07 percent, at 20,129.11. It had surged as high as 20,452.35, encouraged by a rally in Sony Corp and telecoms giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.
"The next focus will be whether the Nikkei rises past the 20,500-21,000 line, where profit-taking is expected to be strong," said Michio Sugita, head of stock trading at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
In Hong Kong, profit-taking set in after nine sessions of rises and the Hang Seng Index met resistance above 14,000.
By the close, the Index was off 81.34 points, or 0.58 percent, at 13,906.46.
Wall Street's gains helped bolster shares in Australia, where pre-budget nerves seemed to be calmed by the overall firm tone of the market. The budget was due at 0930 GMT Tuesday.
The All Ordinaries Index ended 9.5 points higher at 2,534.3, surpassing the previous record closing high of 2,526.0 on May 9.
Elsewhere, a bitter political row over the Taiwan government's ability to fight crime and the extent of an expected cabinet reshuffle put the stock market on hold.
It see-sawed through the morning and ended 14.52 points, or 0.18 percent lower at 7,952.12. The market fell 3.72 percent on Monday as presumed support at 8,000 evaporated.
The cabinet reshuffle was expected to be unveiled at a meeting on Wednesday of the ruling National Party's central standing committee.
Thai shares reversed a recent losing streak as bargain-hunters stepped in to buy blue chips, giving a boost to the local market. It had shed nearly four percent on Monday to drop below the 600 level.
At 1000 GMT, Thai stocks were up 8.06 points, or 1.36 percent, at 600.24.

Analysts said the Thai market was heading into unchartered waters. The recent decision by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh to have a greater role in monitoring the country's economic management was seen clouding the outlook.
Singapore shares took a breather after Monday's advance but traders remained optimistic of further gains.
"There is still a lot of hope that the recent strength may be the upward move we've all been waiting for," one said.
The Straits Times Index was up 11.49 points, or 0.55 percent, at 2,112.97.
Malaysian shares were slightly weaker in thin trading, with the benchmark Composite Index off 3.97 points, or 0.36 percent, at 1,084.55.
Korean stocks recovered after Monday's sell-off, but the market lacked conviction for a rally ahead of Buddha's Birthday on Wednesday, when the market will be closed.
The composite index closed at 683.86, up 11.76 points, or 1.75 percent.
Manila shares ended slightly higher after a see-saw session. The main index up 5.72 points, or 0.21 percent, at 2,677.11.
Indonesian shares were off 2.948 points, or 0.44 percent, at 672.865, while New Zealand shares ended up 2.96 points, or 0.13 percent at 2,303.16.
The dollar steadied against the yen by late afternoon in Tokyo after earlier gains were trimmed by sales from U.S. operators and interbank traders, dealers said.
By 1000 GMT, the dollar stood at 118.80/90 yen from Monday's New York close at 119.30/40, and 1.6980/85 marks from 1.7070/80.
